steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You got the workers and farmers to calm down by having them arm-wrestle as Heraces did? You are a clever one, Titi.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But you already found the solution last night. You just fell asleep in a pile of apples due to exhaustion.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Shame about the apple cider... you were planning to treat the workers and farmers, and get them to work together after they got a little tipsy, weren't you?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Correct. But it's being put to good use to treat an honored guest.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No better medicine for boat sickness, if you're still feeling it! Yia mas!

spans.text: No better medicine for boat sickness, if you're still feeling it!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yia mas!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Oh, so sweet—this is good!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Please, tell me honestly... even though we had the same idea, was it perhaps inappropriate for me to interfere with the rebuilding of the First Temple?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Because you're the Sargonian ambassador?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Because Sargon was—

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Just answer this question, Titi. Do you think the Whitemane King's conquest of Minos was necessary?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Even though it distracted Sargonians from internal strife?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The empire needs to solve its own issues! Blaming it on innocent neighbors is a sign of incompetence.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Although I probably wouldn't be so frank, back in Sargon...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Fine words, fine words! Have another drink! Yamas!

spans.text: Fine words, fine words! Have another drink!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I didn't think a woman so carefree and whimsical would be so pointed when discussing history.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As long as your answer comes from the heart and not concern for your own safety, I think we'll become very good friends.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Priestess Pallas—

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Is this how you address a friend?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Then... Just Pallas. I believe one must not forget oneself, no matter where one goes.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Pepe—a friend of mine back in Sargon—says my train of thought is all over the place and I have no common sense, but that's another matter entirely!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Looks like the Sargon padishahs made a wise choice in picking you to lead the mission...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Don't worry, the workers and farmers are very fond of you. We know a bad egg when we see one, and we don't hate all Sargonians.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Besides, at a time like this, simply participating in the rebuilding of the First Temple is hardly crossing any lines, as long as it helps solve problems.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Look at the pillars, reliefs, and decorations inside the temple. Most of the details are unfinished. The amphitheater outside? There's no slope with the audience seats, so anyone behind the third row can't see what's going on in the center.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And the Kereseira statue that's supposed to be in the middle of the theater? It's still being polished by its perfectionist sculptor.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: A huge-ass problem. No need to weigh your words—it's not like we're writing poetry. Everyone knows that our progress has been way behind schedule.

spans.text: No need to weigh your words—it's not like we're writing poetry. Everyone knows that our progress has been way behind schedule.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Have another drink. Opa!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Now, there's no hard-and-fast deadline. Things will get done eventually, even if the pursuit of perfection keeps delaying things. But a lot of people will be affected, if the delays continue.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The orchard harvests...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Yes. Arm-wrestling and cider might not solve things next time... speaking of cider, you're going through it quickly. Want another cup?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Please! I do have a question, though.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You help the craftsmen solve their problems, and they rely on you. But you don't look concerned at all, even though you're supposed to be the project's supervisor.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hm? No, I wasn't ever the supervisor.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Say what now?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The old tradition only calls for a priest, in this case Kassandra, to give the go-ahead. There is no supervisor for the project itself.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It's not a job for an idle drunk like me. However...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You look like a reasonable gal, and you catch on quick.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: (Takes another swill) Mm...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: What did you say? I was distracted...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No, nothing.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You went through a whole bottle already? You sure can hold your drink. My brew's pretty strong, you know.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Something's not right... didn't you say this cider would help with my boat sickness? I only seem to get dizzier and dizzier...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hey, booze dizziness beats water dizziness, right? Drink until you pass out, and everything will be fine when you wake up the next morning. Including a bit of boat sickness.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Whuh?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I'm sorry, Father, Mother. I've been infected with Oripathy. Your line of work would never let an Infected take over, so now, I'm free to do what I want, right?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I know I can't stay at home any longer. I'll move out as soon as I can. Don't worry about me, I'm able to care for myself now, and I don't need to trouble my family for anything.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: But if it's alright, could you leave my flower garden where it is? They're just plants. Oripathy won't taint them.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Please, let me say goodbye.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: It's been a long time since I last came back to Athenius. Did I forget the way?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: The public garden west of the agora... I should be in the right place. Where's Kassandra?
Did you think a member of the Athenian Council would meet privately with a Rhodes Islander in a public place?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Looks like you've been away for so long that you've forgotten how things work here.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Lydia? It was you who wanted to see me?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I heard you're the Astynomos of Athenius now? I had wanted to catch up with you sometime, but setting up the Rhodes Island branch office took so much time—

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I know. You've done a lot of things for the Infected in the two months that you've been back in Athenius. You could hardly have found the time to come home.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I don't plan on going home, Lydia. They...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Don't worry, you wouldn't run into those vain relatives, even if you went back to the estate.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Two years ago, the Athopoulou family declared bankruptcy and quit the herb business. The remaining family members have since moved out of Athenius.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Looks like you really don't care anymore.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: There isn't much worth remembering about the place, other than my garden.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Your mother used to bring you to play with me in the garden. You came to our house after she passed away.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I taught you about plants and their fragrances. You showed little interest, but you planted the blue boronias with me together, just like the ones here...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You've really forgotten.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Wait... don't tell me, this public garden...

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: This is the flowerbed where you studied and planted medicinal herbs.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Your parents sold the land to the Athenian government to pay off their debts, soon after I became Astynomos.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Did you think they would protect it? Honor the request of the daughter they exiled?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: You've changed, Lydia.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: So have you.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Visiting the Infected, contacting the healing priests, and even reaching out to Kassandra to make sure that veneration of traditional heroism by the Infected would not get in the way of their treatment.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Handling procedure used to be your great weakness. Now, you've learned to circumvent the parts of city administration where the power structure is yet unclear, and go over the head of the new Astynomos.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I see. You didn't come to reminisce about old times. You want to prevent me from talking to the priests—

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: To take the authority to establish and maintain the Infected medical system from the Athenian Council and give it to the Astynomos.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You picked up on that fast.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: It wouldn't be the first time Rhodes Island has dealt with a power-hungry official.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: What Rhodes Island does in an unofficial capacity is none of my business, be it making visits or distributing medicine. You're already doing it, without communication with the Astynomos.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: But you know that changes are coming to Minos, be it the rebuilding of the First Temple, the visit of the Sargonian mission, or the establishment of an Oripathy treatment system.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: The legends of the Minoan heroes are in our blood, but the same traditions have also brought about convoluted governance, inefficient systems, and backward thinking.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You know that better than anyone else.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I want to say you can do whatever you want, as long as an Oripathy treatment system is established, and my patients get what they need.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: But you're the only one in the family I still care about. You're my sister, and I don't want you to put yourself in danger.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Looks like our dear 'ambassador' actually did go strolling off to visit the temple construction site.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: All's well, I suppose. She'll be a fine distraction while I dig into this Astynomos' background. Is the ceremony really delayed, or is she intentionally stalling? If she shows us any disrespect...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Make the preparations. We're going to the Astynomos' Office.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: What? Who's this girl? Guards!

steps.name: Friendly Tourist
steps.text: Beg your pardon, Your Excellency. This is my traveling companion. We hail from Corinia and Lachedamon, invited to attend the ceremony as guests.

steps.name: Friendly Tourist
steps.text: She's passionate about Sargonian culture and insisted on catching a glimpse of the ambassador upon hearing that the mission is lodging here. I couldn't stop her.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: The ambassador... ahem. You have sharp eyes.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You were invited to attend, though? I haven't heard anything from the Astynomos. I understand that the venue of the exchange ceremony has not been confirmed.

steps.name: Friendly Tourist
steps.text: Ah, I shouldn't have babbled, then. Perhaps Lydia intended it to be a surprise.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I am Períandros, priest of Corinia. We learned about the diplomatic mission to Athenius six months ago.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Six months? That long ago?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Yes. The climate of Sargon is very different from that of Minos. Lydia asked me to procure Sargonian-made goods from Corinia in order to make you and the rest of the delegation feel at home.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I hope you are enjoying your accommodations.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Ah, so this was your handiwork.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Lydia has devoted tremendous time and effort to ensuring that the ceremony is a success.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Unfortunately, some of the fabric meant for the costumes for the play have yet to make their way to Hiéreia Kassandra, resulting in a significant delay. Did she mention anything?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: A play... the Astynomos did mention that plays are a part of every important occasion.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: But who is this Hiéreia Kassandra? I thought this matter was entirely managed by the Astynomos' Office.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Ah, it all makes sense now! I almost misunderstood what she meant. No wonder she left specific instructions not to use the traditional fabric for classical plays. I'm so grateful for the heads-up.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The cotton used for this event is a hybrid of Sargonian and Minoan species. They make a smooth and strong cloth that signifies the lasting peace between our two nations. That's why Lydia insisted on waiting.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I see. So this is the reason she delayed the ceremony...

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Delayed? I'm so sorry about that. I really apologize for the trouble. I hope you will not take Lydia's best intentions the wrong way.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Very well. It would be impolite to rush her, if she is taking this ceremony so seriously. Thank you for bringing this to my attention.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: You're too kind. Please, make yourselves at home for a few days while preparations for the ceremony continue.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Don't look at me like that. I came with you when you made three rounds of the food stalls in the morning. Only fair that you should come with me here.

steps.name: Stray Tourist
steps.text: How much of what you said was actually true?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The Sargonian delegation has entered the city, and the Astynomos invited us to attend the ceremony, but she didn't tell us anything about her arrangements. What choice do I have but to figure this out on my own?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I assuaged his concerns for her, didn't I?

steps.name: Stray Tourist
steps.text: The merchants of Corinia would not be famous throughout Terra, if profit were the only thing on their minds.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Now, now, it's not polite to say that out loud.
